title: Avoid shell=True when launching editor with filenames in Editor.edit_files

note.title: Avoid shell=True when launching editor with filenames in Editor.edit_files
answers: Why does click.edit fail or behave unexpectedly with filenames containing quotes or spaces?
How should editor commands be executed without shell=True in Editor.edit_files?
How to prevent command injection when opening files in external editors?
note.body:
Symptom: Opening files with quotes, spaces, or shell metacharacters in an external editor causes syntax errors or executes arbitrary shell commands.
Root cause: `src/click/_termui_impl.py:Editor.edit_files` formatted filenames into a command string and invoked `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=True`.
Fix pattern: Split the editor command string with `shlex.split()` and append filenames as discrete argument list items to `subprocess.Popen` without `shell=True`.
Constraints: Applies when launching external editors via subprocess; editor command string must be split into argv before appending filename arguments.
note.applies: Invoking user-configured editor commands via subprocess in click._termui_impl.
